links.note: Suffrage as the right to vote - the franchise is discussed inside the liberalism section (property-owning men only, briefly all adult males under the Jacobins), so 23844.

The 1833 Hamburg-to-Nuremberg merchant passing 11 customs barriers is the illustration of liberalism in the economic sphere - freedom of markets and the abolition of state-imposed restrictions on the movement of goods, which 23844 names.

Napoleon's defeat in 1815 is the opening of the new-conservatism passage ('following the defeat of Napoleon in 1815, European governments were driven by a spirit of conservatism'), so 23845. Not the Napoleon sub-section, which this frame has no concept for.
Conservatism as preserving monarchy, Church, social hierarchies, property and family is the definition in the post-1815 conservative-order passage, 23845.
The Treaty of Constantinople 1832 recognising Greece as independent - the Greek war is one of 23845's revolts against the conservative order. The same item as qid:106109, which has no key marked.

Louis Philippe fleeing and the National Assembly proclaiming a Republic in 1848 is the February 1848 events, 23846 - the revolution in which the liberals' demands ran alongside the revolts of the poor.
Bismarck as the chief architect of Prussian-led German unification - 23847.

Garibaldi (1807-82) as the most celebrated Italian freedom fighter - 23848, which names Mazzini, Cavour and Garibaldi. The distractors include Mazzini, so the item turns on telling the Italian figures apart.
Russia, Germany, England and Austro-Hungary each countering the others' hold on the Balkans as a major cause of the First World War is 23852's description exactly.
